summary: The deterministic macro backdrop remains growth-positive but risk-sensitive. No newer official U.S. CPI/Core CPI, PCE/Core PCE, NFP/unemployment, ISM, Taiwan PMI/NMI, export-orders, leading-indicator or central-bank release superseded the repository observations in this run. Material new information came from two directions: China's August exports accelerated to 25.0% y/y, supporting regional AI/high-tech demand, while the Middle East conflict escalated into direct attacks on Saudi energy facilities, pushing Brent briefly to $99.46 and WTI to $94.73 and increasing the probability that energy, refined-product and freight inflation remain persistent. Russia also resumed major strikes on Kyiv after a temporary diplomatic pause.

geopolitical_global_risk.summary: Observed evidence worsened materially from September 7: Iran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi energy facilities and cities, Saudi authorities reported 73 wounded, some energy operations were halted, and Hormuz traffic remained below normal. Brent reached $99.46 intraday and WTI $94.73. Separately, Russia resumed large-scale attacks on Kyiv after the temporary pause surrounding U.S.-mediated talks. Semantic interpretation: the Middle East shock now carries a higher probability of persistent imported-inflation, freight and rate pressure for Taiwan, while the Russia-Ukraine channel remains a secondary refined-product and European-demand risk.

key_risks: Direct attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure increase the probability that the Middle East shock persists through crude, refined products and shipping rather than remaining a short-lived risk premium.
Brent near $100 and record-high diesel/gasoline conditions raise imported-inflation and margin pressure for Taiwan before the next U.S. inflation release and FOMC decision.
U.S. 10-year yields near 4.8% raise duration risk for technology and other long-duration equities.
China's export strength supports Taiwan's AI/high-tech demand channel but also raises the probability of additional trade barriers aimed at Chinese industrial surpluses.
Russia's renewed Kyiv strikes reduce the near-term de-escalation signal from recent diplomacy and keep refined-product/European-growth risk active.
U.S.-China semiconductor tariffs and export controls remain a persistent structural risk for Taiwan technology supply chains.
